reply.subject: RM_SparkleechGrub

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. South is the grub seen end-on from the front, with a big ringed, fleshy pink circular mouth opening into a dark bore in the centre, surrounded by cream segmented body rings and stubby nub legs at the bottom. East is a long side profile: tapering segmented cream body, about 9 rings, short nub prolegs along the belly, a tapered tail at left and an open tube-like pink socket mouth at right. North is the rear end-on: concentric segment rings narrowing to a blunt tail tip, nub legs at the base, and no mouth, face or eyes.
observed.south.png: Front view, end-on: a round pink corrugated ring-mouth with a dark hollow centre, framed by pale beige mottled segments and small bulbous feet. Painterly with soft shading, on clean alpha.
observed.east.png: Side profile of a segmented maggot-like body, cream with grey-green mottling. The head end on the right is an open cylindrical socket ringed in pink, and the tail tapers to the left. Six or seven small rounded prolegs. Clean alpha with no shadow.
observed.north.png: Rear view: a stacked dome of segment rings converging on a tapered tail point, with nub feet at the bottom corners. No face. Slightly taller than the south view.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the grub is a small pale segmented sliver about a third of a cell long, far smaller than the human. At 32 px/cell it is a tiny pale fleck beside the rat, barely visible.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head end-on, with the socket mouth facing the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the tapered tail end in concentric rings, with no mouth or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three views are at the low game-camera angle. None looks down on the back.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 86% height spread comes from the pose. The end-on views (south/north) show the body's full cross-section stacked vertically, and the long east profile is low and long. East width (~470 px) against end-on width (~260 px) matches one elongated body. North is about 10% taller than south, which is minor.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same cream mottled palette, segment rings and nub prolegs appear on all facings. The socket mouth shows on south and on the east head end and is absent on north, so it turns with the body.

SIGNATURE.seen: The socket-mouthed grub is very legible: a ringed tubular mouth with a dark bore on south and east. It is low to the ground with short legs.

ALIEN.seen: The def names a grub, so a grub body is allowed (earth_body_named: yes). The socket mouth sets it apart from a plain maggot.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1. Socket-shaped mouth: present. It is a pink corrugated tube opening on south and on the east head.

STYLE.seen: Painterly mottled skin texture with soft realistic shading. No cute eyes and no cel shading.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art with a socket mouth. Not vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: Clean checkerboard around all facings. No ground patch or shadow.

SCALE.seen: About a third of a cell next to the human, which fits drawSize 0.32 and a small grub.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it is a tiny pale fleck that barely separates from the ground. The mouth and segments are unreadable.

reply.image_seen: The facing sheet and individual sprites show a cream segmented grub with a circular socket mouth in south and east, a tapered closed rear in north, and a small body beside the human in the scale panel.

concerns.evidence: On the shared-scale facing sheet, north and south have comparable body widths and segment thicknesses. North's additional vertical extent follows its elongated, tapered rear silhouette; south ends in a broad socket mouth. This supports a difference in projected anatomy rather than an overall enlargement. East's low profile likewise explains the large measured height spread.
